The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act 1996 and requested this Court to set aside the common Arbitral Award dated 10.03.2020 passed in case No.LAQ/ARB/NH-04/CR/6H/2009-10.
.2.
In the petition it is stated that National Highways Authority of India was constituted by an Act of the Parliament, "the National Highways Authority of A.P. No.100/2021 India Act, 1988" .

entities.text: National Highways Authority of A.P. No.100/2021 India Act, 1988
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is responsible for the development, maintenance and management of National Highways entrusted to it and for matters connected or incidental thereto.

.3. It is stated that the Central Government for the purpose of widening of NH-4 on the stretch of land from 10 to kms. 29.50 of Bengaluru-Nelamangala Section issued preliminary Notification dated 22.11.2006 (1 st Stage if acquisition) under Section 3-A(1) of the National Highways Act, 1956 in-respect of acquisition of lands situated at Chikkabidrakallu village, Dasanapura Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluka.

The final notification was published in the official Gazette on 13.11.2007.
.4.

It is stated that under the said notification for the 1st stage of acquisition, amongst other lands the Non-agricultural (NA) lands in Sy.No.24/2 to an extent of 110.3 Sq. Mtrs. equivalent to 1,188Sq.
ft., situated at the said Village belonging to the 1 st Respondent were also acquired.

It is stated that in accordance with Section 3(a) of the NH Act, the respondent No. 3 was A.P. No.100/2021 appointed as the competent authority by the Central Government.
.5.
It is stated that the respondent No.3 vide award dated 10.04.2008 determined the market value of NA lands at Rs.250/- per sq. ft.

In order to determine compensation, the 3rd respondent had procured from the office of the Sub-Registrar, Bangalore North Taluk, the Sales Statistics from 23.11.2005 to 22.11.2006 (preceding one year) and the Guidance Value for the relevant period for both agricultural and Non- agricultural (NA) lands in the said Village.

The respondent No. 3 after examining both and after conducting spot inspection opined that the sale statistics was not in consonance with the prevailing market value and hence relied upon the guidance value and determined the market value of NA lands at Rs.250/- per Sq.ft.
Being dissatisfied with the amount awarded by Respondent No.3, the 1st Respondent approached the 2nd Respondent under Section 3-G(5) of the NH Act.

2 A.P. No.100/2021 .6.
It is stated that the petitioner entered appearance and filed its Statement of objections with documents as well as written submissions with several Judgments in support of its defence.

The 2 nd Respondent has enhanced the market value from Rs.250/- per Sq. ft to Rs.962/-
per Sq. ft. by treating them as commercial lands abutting National Highway.

The Preliminary Notification in respect of Chikkabidrakallu village was published on 22nd November 2006 whereas, the Notification relied upon the 2nd Respondent came into effect from 19th April 2007 i.e., after a lapse of more than 5 months from the date of publication of Preliminary Notification.
Hence, the Respondent could not have relied upon the same for the purpose of enhancement compensation.

(e) The respondent No.2 has held that as per the aforesaid Notification, the guidance value of agricultural lands situated at Chikkabidrakallu Village was Rs.1,50,00,000/- Acre, NA lands was Rs.425/- per Sq. ft and that of Gramathana was Rs. 350/- per Sq.ft.
In order to re- A.P. No.100/2021 determine the market value of NA lands, the 2nd respondent taken the rate of Rs.1,50,00,000/- per acre equivalent to Rs.344/- per Sq. ft. as the basis.
Thereafter the 2nd Respondent has added 60% on the same and arrived at Rs.550/-.

(f) Further the 2nd Respondent has concluded that since the acquired lands are abutting NH and commercial in nature, further 75% has to be added on Rs.550/- and arrived at Rs.962/- per Sq. ft.
i.e. Rs.550/- + Rs.412/- (75% of Rs. 550/-).

(g) It is relevant to mention here that the entry at page No.288 Sl. No.15 provides for guidance value of NA lands situated at Chikkabidrakallu Village as Rs.425/- per Sq. ft. but Sl.No.15 (a) does not provide for guidance value of NA lands abutting NH.

On one hand the 2nd Respondent has stated at page 7 of the Arbitral award that the guidance value of NA lands of Chikkabidrakallu village is A.P./100/2021 on 2 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8778494/
3 Rs.425/-per Sq. ft.
But nowhere has relied upon the said rate in so far as NA land are concerned.

Consequently, the statement of the 2 nd Respondent that the enhancement is made A.P.
No.100/2021 on the basis of the Notification dated 17 th April 2007 is completely false.
(h) There is absolutely no justification for the addition of 60% and 75% which renders the impugned Arbitral award completely illegal.
The Notification dated 17th April 2007 is a document which did not form a part of the Arbitral proceedings and the Petitioner was never given an opportunity to rebut the same.
Hence the impugned Arbitral award is contrary to provisions of Section 24 of the A and C Act.
(i) The impugned Arbitral award is not a speaking order and liable to be set aside.

The 2nd respondent has neither complied with the procedure provided under Section 24, nor decided the dispute in accordance with Section 28(1)(a) and at the same time has failed to comply with Section 31(3) of the A & C Act, thus rendering the impugned Arbitral award opposed to settled position of law.
A.P. No.100/2021 (j) The signed copy of the impugned Arbitral award was never served upon the Petitioner.

The 2nd respondent has violated the provision of Section 31(5) of the A & C Act.
.8.
The petitioner submits that the impugned Arbitral award was passed on 10th March 2020.
The copy of the impugned arbitral award was received for the first time by the Petitioner on 27th November 2020 through the 3rd Respondent.

Petition is being filed in accordance with the order passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Suo Moto W.P.(Civil)3/2020 excluding the period of limitation period between 15 th March 2020 till 14th March 2021.
Hence, the petition is in time.

.9. The respondent No.1 has filed objections submitting that the arbitrator was appointed by the Central Government and the arbitrator was experienced in Revenue matters and the Authority to decide the market value of the land in question in various land acquisition proceedings initiated by the State Government.
He having found, that the market value A.P. No.100/2021 decided by the respondent No.3 is on lower side has passed the award and enhanced the compensation.
The finding of the arbitrator in so far as giving enhancement concerned is a question of fact which cannot taken up as cause for filing the above petition by the petitioner.
Hence the petition is liable to be rejected.
The above petition filed by the petitioner is not within the time prescribed under law and barred by limitation.
Hence the petition itself is not maintainable either in law and facts of the case.

.10. The following points that would arise for my consideration are:
(1) Whether petitioner in A.P. No.100/2021 has made out sufficient grounds under Section 34 of Arbitration and Conciliation Act to set aside the arbitral award dated 10.03.2020 passed by respondent No.2?
(2) What order or award?

My findings on the above points are:
Point No.1 : In the Negative Point No.2 : As per final order, for the following:
REASONS .12. POINT No.1:

The respondent No. 3 has acquired the NA land in Sy.No. 24/2 to an extent of 110.3 sq. meters equivalent to 1,188 sq. feet situated at Chikkabidarakallu village under the preliminary notification dated 22.11.2006.
The respondent No. 3 has determined the market value of NA lands at Rs.250/- per sq. ft.
The respondent No. 1 being dissatisfied with the award amount had approached the respondent No. 2 under Section 3-G(5) of NH Act.
The respondent No. 2 has re-determined the the market value at Rs. 962/- per sq. ft.
Being aggrieved by the said award, the petitioner has filed this petition under Section 34 of Arbitration and Conciliation Act.
It is necessary to bear in mind the scope of this Court to interfere with the award passed by the Arbitrator.
Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 provide the circumstances under which an award can be set aside by a civil Court.

Explanation shows that an award is in conflict with the pubic policy of India (i) if the making of the award was induced or affected by fraud or corruption or was in violation of Section 75 or Section 81.

(ii) It A.P.
No.100/2021 is in conflict with contravention with the fundamental policy of Indian Law or (iii) It is in conflict with most basic notion of morality or justice.
Explanation 2. The test as to whether there is contravention with the fundamental policy of Indian law shall not entail a review on the merits of the dispute.

2A It may also be set aside if the Court finds the award is vitiated by patent illegality appearing on the face of award provided that an award shall not be set aside merely on the ground of an erroneous application of law or by re appreciation of evidence.

5
Bearing in mind the above section, now it has to be seen whether the impugned award suffers from any patent error illegality as envisage in the above section.
14. The petitioner has stated that the respondent No.3 Arbitrator has relied upon the notification dated 17.04.2007 which came into effect from 19.04.2007.
Preliminary notification in the present case was issued A.P. No.100/2021 on 22.11.2006.

It is stated that as per Substantial Law NH Authority Act Section 3-G(7)(a), the arbitrator while determining the amount shall take into consideration the market value of the land as on the date of publication of the notification under Section 3-A of NH Act.

It is argued that the respondent No.2 could not have relied upon the guidelines value which came into effect after publication of preliminary notification dated 22.11.2006.
15.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Oil & Natural Gas Corp. Ltd., Vs. SAW Pipes Ltd. (AIR 2003 SC 2629) has held that:
 "if the award is contrary to the  Substantive provisions of law or the provisions of the Act or against the terms of the contract, it would be patently illegal, which could be interfered under Section 34".
A.P. No.100/2021 16.

sentences.text: If at all the Arbitrator relied on the notification dated 17.04.2007, the respondent No. 2 should have deescalated the value to the date of preliminary notification.

17. As per Rule No.5 of the Karnataka Stamps Constitution of Central valuation committee for estimation, publication and revision of market value guidelines of property rules 2003 deals with estimation of market value guidelines.

As per the said guidance the central valuation committee shall as far as possible in the first week of October of every calendar year send instruction along with general policy guidelines to all the committees in the state of estimation of market value guidelines of properties for the next calendar year.
Such instructions may be sent to any sub committee at any time of the calendar year for the revision of the rates, if required.

18. Rule 7 of the above Karnataka Stamp rules states that the Secretary of the Central Valuation Committee on receipt of statement from the Registrar of A.P. No.100/2021 a district shall verify and place them before the committee which shall meet in the third week of January in the next calendar year.

Sub rule 3 states that on approval of the estimation of the each sub district/district, the statements shall be attested by the secretary on behalf of the committee who shall then send such approved statements of estimation of market value of properties to the Registrar of the districts in the 1st week of the March in the next calendar year and later shall forward it to the concerned sub committee within the week of the receipt of the statements in such form as may be specified by the committee from time to time.

From the above rules it is clear that the process for fixing the guidelines value has commenced in the October 2006; that actually the market value of the property for the year 2006 which was published in 2007.

In circumstances reliance placed on the guidance value notification dated 17-04-2007 for reckoning the market value of the property acquired under A.P. No.100/2021 preliminary notification dated 22-11-2006 by itself cannot be accepted to be a patent illegality committed by the 2nd respondent arbitrator.

20. The Arbitrator relying upon the guidelines value dated 17.04.2007 has redetermined the market value at Rs. 962/- per sq. ft.

The petitioner has stated that the guidance value of agricultural land situated at Chikkabidarakallu village was Rs. 1,50,00,000/- per acre, NA lands was Rs. 425/- per sq. feet and that of gramathana was Rs. 350/- per sq. feet.

In order to re-determine the market value for NA lands, the respondent No. 2 has taken the rate of agricultural land at Rs. 1,50,00,000/- per acre,
equivalent to Rs. 344/- per sq. feet.
He added 60% on the same and arrived at Rs.550/-.
Thereafter,

550/- per sq. feet and arrived at Rs. 962/- per sq. feet.
22.
It is stated that the entry at page No. 288, Sl. No. 15 provides that the guidance value of NA lands situated at Chikkabidarakallu village at Rs.425/- per sq.ft.
It does not provide for guidance value of NA lands abutting NH.

The special instruction to the said notification provides that 50% and 25% is to be added on the guidance for lands abutting NH and State Highway respectively when the A.P./100/2021 on 2 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8778494/
7 guidance value of particular property is not specifically provided for under the notification.
The arbitrator had not relied upon the rate in so far as value of lands NA lands are concerned.
It would have been open for the arbitrator to take note of the value fixed for the commercial/gramatna sites.

It is stated that there is no justification for addition of A.P. No.100/2021 60% for NA, 75% on NH and commercial lands on Rs. 1,50,00,000/- per acre.

.25. The proviso to Sub Section (2A) of Section 34 of Act of 1996, clearly indicates that "An award shall not be set aside merely on the ground of erroneous application of law."

sentences.text: In view of the above decision and the section 34(2) of the A and C Act the above contention of the petitioner cannot be examined.
.26. The Arbitrator has relied upon guidelines value dated 17.04.2007.
This document is not valid record received from the Arbitrator as none of the A.P. No.100/2021 parties have produced and this is evident from the record of the Arbitrator.
Section 24(3) of the Act provides provision regarding hearing and written proceedings.

It reads thus:
"All statements, documents or other information supplied to, or applications made to the arbitral tribunal by one party shall be communicated to the other party, and any expert report or evidentiary document on which the arbitral tribunal may rely in making its decision shall be communicated to the parties".
27. As the Arbitrator has relied on the estimated guidelines value of immovable properties and buildings dated 17.04.2007 without bringing to the knowledge of the parties and thereby has failed to follow the procedure under Section 24 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act.
So the award has to be set aside on the ground of patent illegality.

28. The petitioner has contended that the respondent No.2 has not assigned any reasons for re- determining the compensation nor he has assigned any A.P. No.100/2021 reasons for enhancing the compensation or for relying upon notification dated 17.04.2007.
29.

In Som Dutt Builders Ltd Vs. State of Kerala (2010)2 AWC (supp) 1390 SC) has held that:
"Reasons must be indicated in the award as that would reflect thought process leading to a particular conclusion.

31. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Oil & Natural Gas Corp. Ltd. Vs. SAW Piles Ltd., (AIR 2003 SC 2629) has held that:
A.P. No.100/2021 "if the award is patently against the statutory provisions of Substantive law which is in force in India or is passed without giving an opportunity of hearing to the parties as provided under Section 24 or without giving any reason in a case where parties have not agreed that no reasons are to be recorded, it would be against the statutory provisions.

In all such cases, the award is required to be set aside on the ground of 'patent illegality'
32.

The L.A.O. and Arbitrator has not taken into consideration additional market value of 12%, 30%
solatium and 15% interest on additional market value and solatium.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court has in AIR 2019 SC 4689: AIR Online 2019 SC 1087 - Union of India and another Vs. Tarsem Singh and others has held that:
"provisions of Land Acquisition Act relating to solatium and interest contained in S.23(1A) and (2) and interest payable in terms of Section 28 proviso - will apply to acquisitions made under National Highways Act - Consequently, S. 3-J to extent of granting compensation without solatium and interest - Is violative of Art. 14 of Constitution and, therefore, declared to be unconstitutional.

34. Though the Arbitrator has not complied with Section 28 and 31 of A and C Act.
Endeavor of the Court should be honour and support the award as far as possible.
The acquisition is of the year 2006.
There is error committed by the Arbitrator in passing the award.

Since 12% additional market value, 30% solatium and thereafter 15% till deposit has not been given by L.A.O, I feel if the same is given the compensation which respondent No. 1 would get more or less be the same as awarded by Arbitrator.
For the said reason I do not intend to interfere with the award passed by the respondent No.2.
Hence, I answer point No.1 in the Negative 35.

Point No.2: In view of the aforesaid finding on point No.1 I proceed to pass the following:

The impugned award passed by the respondent No.2 in so far as pertaining to case No.LAQ/ARB/NH-4/CR/6H/2009-10 is confirmed.

Endeavor of the Court should be honour and support the award as far as possible.
The acquisition is of the year 2006.
There is error committed by the Arbitrator in passing the award.

For the said reason I do not intend to interfere with the award passed by the respondent No.2.
Hence, I answer point No.1 in the Negative 35.
